The Kinetiq pages, last updated 25 November and 2 November 2026, now describe what the announced ArbOS upgrade adds: a HyperCore read precompile and an ElysiumCoreWriter predeploy that holds HYPE gas escrows and delivers asynchronous result callbacks to the contract that emitted an intent.

deltas.delta: The ElysiumCoreWriter predeploy and a keeper lane ship in an ArbOS network upgrade about four weeks after mainnet. A dapp contract binds its HyperCore account on the predeploy, may prefund a HYPE gas escrow there, and receives each action's outcome as an on-chain callback paid from that escrow.
The HyperCore data precompile makes orderbooks, prices, balances and positions readable by any contract for call gas, as a post-launch upgrade.

findings.title: Elysium's announced ArbOS upgrade adds a HyperCore read precompile and a callback predeploy whose addresses and call shapes are not yet published
findings.difference: Kinetiq states that an ArbOS upgrade about four weeks after mainnet adds a native precompile that returns live HyperCore state, balances included, and an ElysiumCoreWriter predeploy that keeps per-contract HYPE escrows and calls contracts back with the result of each HyperCore action. Neither exists on Ethereum, and neither is in the 36 precompiles the node lists today.
findings.mechanism: The PoolManager reaches a new address in four shapes only. sync(X) staticcalls X.balanceOf(PoolManager) and settle credits the rise of that word as currency X (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288 and 349-364). take(X, to, amount) calls X.transfer(to, amount) and accepts empty return data or a 32 byte one (src/types/Currency.sol:53-80). take(address(0), X, amount) sends value with empty calldata (src/types/Currency.sol:44-52). A hook address with valid low flag bits receives the IHooks selectors (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:109-124 and 131-160). If the read precompile answered the balanceOf selector with a word that moves, an account could book that movement as a delta of currency X, but X is the precompile address, which no pool of real tokens names, so the booked credit is worth nothing to other users. A value call into the predeploy that it treats as an escrow deposit is paid by the caller of take, who is debited the full amount. A result callback goes to the contract that emitted the intent; the PoolManager cannot emit one, because none of its four call shapes carries caller-chosen calldata to an address other than the hook. The hazard therefore rests on the precompile or predeploy answering one of these selectors in a way the published text does not describe.
findings.impact: None found today. Recorded so that the day-one check of the upgrade calls both new addresses from the PoolManager address in the four shapes above.
findings.preconditions: Elysium governance must ship the upgrade; nothing is scheduled at block 11,231,491.
findings.mitigations: After activation, run the cycle 16 precompile sweep against the new addresses from the PoolManager address, and check whether either address has low 14 bits that form a valid hook flag set.

leads.question: When Elysium activates the HyperCore upgrade, what do the read precompile and the ElysiumCoreWriter predeploy return to a balanceOf(PoolManager) staticcall, a transfer(address,uint256) call and an empty-calldata value call from the PoolManager address, and do their addresses have low 14 bits that form a valid hook flag set?
leads.why: A balance word that moves would be bookable through sync and settle, and a predeploy that accepts transfer with empty return data would let take succeed without moving anything (src/types/Currency.sol:53-80).
